subject: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a working Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the 8-week pilot and a short note on how we think SLA/latency SLOs should map to commercial concessions. The goal here is to make tradeoffs explicit so procurement and engineering can sign off quickly.

High-level MAP (attached: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff & infra access (VPC peering + sample dataset)
- Week 2–4: Evaluation phase — run standard eval suite (attached: Acme_Eval_Criteria.xlsx) and 72-hour production-like soak on a representative slice
- Week 5: Post-eval review and acceptance decision (pass/fail + a short defects list)
- Week 6–8: Pilot ramp to committed qps and final commercial terms + DocuSign

Commercial concessions tied to milestones (proposal):
- If evaluation acceptance criteria met at Week 5: 20% one-time pilot discount on first three months OR $X in usage credits (Acme to choose)
- If pilot ramps to committed QPS within Week 6–8: additional 10% discount on committed tier for first 6 months
- If evaluation fails: no penalties, we capture learnings and provide a 30-day extension at the same pilot rate to try again

SLOs and measurement (critical):
- We propose operational latency SLOs only for the committed tier after pilot closes (pilot is best-effort).
- Example commitment: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 850ms for typical 512-token requests measured over a 30-day rolling window on the committed capacity.
- Degradation clause: if p99 exceeds 1200ms for >5% of a 7-day window, we trigger a joint review and agreed remediation plan; commercial credit applies only if Redwood cannot restore target SLO within the escalation window AND the incident is within Redwood’s control plane/serving runtime (not customer-side network issues).

Measurements and proof:
- All SLO calculations will use Redwood Console telemetry tied to token-level traces and per-route histograms (we will share access to a read-only dashboard).
- Accepted incidents will be backed by trace ids and sample requests; we will provide a runbook for evidence collection.

Next steps: please review the attached MAP and SLA term sheet and let us know the names for your technical verifier (for access) and procurement contact for redlines. Rishi will follow up with a pricing summary keyed to committed QPS.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: Acme_Eval_Criteria.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Priya —

Thanks for the clear MAP. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we share with procurement: 
1) The SLO numbers (p95/p99) look reasonable, but procurement is asking how those map to credits/discounts quantitatively. Can you provide a simple table: percentage credit vs. missed SLO buckets?
2) Can we get the read-only dashboard access during Week 2 so our verifier (Tom) can observe metrics in near-real-time?
3) On the "committed QPS" — we expect to commit to 250 QPS at the end of the pilot, ramp to 1k over 3 months. Is Redwood comfortable with the ramp schedule for the discount to kick in?

Also attaching our initial procurement template with some redlines around liability and data retention.

- Sarah
Director, AI Platforms
Acme Corp
[Attachment: procurement_template_acme_redlines.docx (DOCX)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Team —

Per Sarah's questions, here's a pragmatic pricing/playbook we can offer. This keeps the MAP simple and ties commercial downside to objective SLO misses.

Proposed SLO-credit table (applies to committed tier, not pilot):
- p99 within target (<=850ms): 0% monthly credit
- p99 between 850ms and 1200ms: 5% monthly credit for each week the window falls into that bucket (capped at 20% per month)
- p99 > 1200ms for >5% of any 7-day window: 15% credit for that month AND remediation plan required

Discounts tied to ramp/commit: 
- Pilot acceptance (Week 5): one-time 20% pilot discount (or $50k credit)
- Commit to 250 QPS within Week 8: addl. 8% off committed tier for first 6 months
- Ramp to >=1k QPS within 90 days: further 7% on top of the above for months 4–6

Notes / constraints:
- Credits are calculated on subscription/committed spend only, not on overage.
- SLO calculations exclude known customer-side network impairments (forwarding traces required).
- We will instrument a joint SLO dashboard and a lightweight 'SLO acceptance test' during Week 6 to baseline p95/p99 on representative traffic.

Marissa — can CS own the dashboard share and the wrap-up runbook? Vivek — please confirm the p99 measurement definition matches runtime histograms (512 tokens, model X-quantized).

Rishi

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Sarah / Tom —

Thanks — attached is a clean term-sheet that encodes Rishi's SLO-credit table and the ramp-linked discounts. Also included is a DocuSign placeholder we can activate once procurement confirms redlines: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC-ACME-2026

Short summary for procurement: 
- Pilot period: 8 weeks, acceptance at Week 5 required for pilot discount to apply.
- Measurement: p95/p99 measured via Redwood Console; SLO credits apply only to committed monthly subscription.
- Ramp: commit to 250 QPS to unlock the first tier discount; larger discounts tied to hitting 1k within 90 days.
- Liability/data retention: per our standard enterprise addendum; see attached redline doc.

If procurement confirms they can accept the SLO-credit buckets and data retention language, we'll prep the final contract and send DocuSign. Can you confirm the verifier (Tom) access request so Marissa can share the dashboard?

Best,
Priya

From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Priya —

Procurement has a couple of redlines on the SLA-credit table and the liability cap. Specific asks:
1) Replace percentage credits with flat-dollar credits for clarity (we proposed $X/day for p99 breaches above threshold).
2) Narrow the definition of "within Redwood control" — exclude managed infra (cloud provider outages) but include runtime regressions, and require a 48-hour remediation SLA before credits apply.
3) We need standard indemnity language and a 12-month data retention maximum.

We can accept the MAP milestones otherwise. Please have legal/finance propose language on item (1) and (2) so we can move to signatures this week.

Thanks,
Acme Procurement
[Attachment: procurement_template_acme_redlines.docx (DOCX)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial MAP & SLO tradeoffs — Acme pilot

Hi all —

Quick technical clarification to resolve the "within Redwood control" language that procurement asked about. We propose the following, which tracks our operational responsibilities and what we can instrument: 

- "Redwood control" includes: serving runtime kernel regressions, model packaging regressions, routing errors inside Redwood's network boundary, and misconfigurations in the Redwood-managed inference stack.
- Excludes: public cloud provider region-wide networking outages, customer-side network/firewall misconfigurations, and downstream third-party model-response transformations executed on the customer side.

Operational commitments and evidence: 
- When an SLO incident is claimed, Redwood will: (a) provide trace ids and per-request histograms within 24 hours, (b) run a root-cause analysis (RCA) within 5 business days, and (c) enact hotfix or rollback within the agreed escalation windows where applicable.
- If RCA shows issue was in Redwood control, credits apply per the agreed table; if not, we will propose a mitigations plan but no credits.

Measurement note: our p99 numbers are computed on the model inference latency excluding pre-signing and post-processing latency (we will show component-level breakdowns in the dashboard). The 512-token baseline matters; if you test at much larger payloads we'll need to re-baseline SLOs.

I'll work with Marissa to give Tom read-only dashboard access by EOD tomorrow and will ask infra to prepare a 24-hour synthetic run so we have a baseline sample.

- Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
